correctness.rationale: For a total dominating set in the bipartite incidence graph, selected points meet every affine hyperplane and selected hyperplanes cover every point, including selected vertices. Brouwer–Schrijver 1978 proves the exact point-blocking lower bound d(q-1)+1 for finite-field affine spaces. Counting q^(d-1) points per hyperplane gives the sharp cover bound q. Coordinate axes B and the parallel class x_1=c achieve total domination. A paired set has equal-sized selected point and hyperplane parts because its matching is bipartite, so the blocking bound doubles; the explicitly listed coordinate hyperplanes support a bijective perfect matching with B. Independent finite-field constructions and exhaustive small-plane verification support every step. Not asserted for non-Desarguesian planes.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Projective-plane incidence graphs and edge domination do not imply the new full affine point-hyperplane total and paired numerical values. General paired-domination bounds do not give equality or the matching construction. The 1978 theorem provides only a proper input; it has no graph matched-pair claim.

value.rationale: Exact unbounded separation (d-1)(q-1) of two natural strengthened guard parameters on the canonical connected point–hyperplane incidence family of all finite affine spaces. The gap has a sharp structural explanation in the equal-sided perfect-matching requirement and an explicit construction realizing the blocking lower bound, rather than being a substitution into a pre-existing paired-domination formula. The 1978 blocking theorem itself is fully credited.
